skill.name: web-browser
skill.description: Controls a local Chrome browser through CDP to navigate pages, run page JavaScript, capture screenshots, and select elements.
skill.summary: Local Chrome automation helpers for navigation, screenshots, page evaluation, and element selection.
skill.author: Dwsy

security_audit.summary: The skill provides useful local Chrome automation, but it includes high-risk behavior around browser profile copying, hidden profile storage, fixed CDP control, and arbitrary page evaluation. Many markdown, template-literal, and example-URL detections are false positives, while child_process use, rsync profile copying, CDP access, and sensitive browser data handling are confirmed.

remediation.issue: The profile option copies cookies, logins, and other Chrome profile data into ~/.cache/scraping.
remediation.suggestion: Disable profile copying by default, require explicit user confirmation, and document that copied profiles contain sensitive session data.

remediation.issue: Chrome is launched with a fixed remote debugging port and a reusable user data directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use a fresh temporary profile, choose a random local port per run, bind to localhost explicitly, and shut Chrome down after use.

remediation.issue: start.js uses shell commands for killall, mkdir, and rsync.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell calls with Node filesystem APIs and spawn commands with argument arrays. Avoid shell interpolation of environment-derived paths.

remediation.issue: eval.js executes arbitrary JavaScript supplied on the command line in the active page.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer allow-listed inspection helpers or require explicit confirmation before evaluating custom JavaScript on authenticated pages.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Profile Copying Exposes Authenticated Sessions
semantic_findings.description: The documentation advertises copying cookies and logins with the profile option, and start.js rsyncs the default Chrome profile into ~/.cache/scraping. Running that copied profile under CDP can expose authenticated sessions to local browser automation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The SKILL.md text explicitly says the profile option copies cookies and logins, and the code performs a full Chrome profile rsync. The same profile is used by a remotely controlled Chrome instance.

semantic_findings.title: Unauthenticated Local CDP Browser Control
semantic_findings.description: The skill starts Chrome on port 9222 and helper scripts connect to that endpoint for navigation, screenshots, element inspection, and page JavaScript evaluation. Any local process with access to that endpoint can control the browser context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation and start script identify the fixed CDP port, and eval.js demonstrates active page code execution through that browser session. The risk depends on local access but is directly supported by the code.

content.value_statement: Manual web checks are slow when an AI assistant needs page context. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code local Chrome controls for navigation, screenshots, evaluation, and element selection.
actual_capabilities: Starts a local Google Chrome instance with Chrome DevTools Protocol remote debugging.
Navigates the current browser tab or opens a new tab for a supplied URL.
Runs JavaScript expressions in the active page and prints returned values.
Captures the current viewport as a screenshot file in the system temporary directory.
Lets the user click page elements and returns selected tag, text, class, HTML, and parent details.
limitations: The start script expects the macOS Google Chrome application path.
The helper scripts require a Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint on localhost port 9222.
The profile option can copy cookies and logins, so it is unsafe for sensitive accounts.
The skill does not provide sandboxing, authentication, or remote browser isolation.

use_cases.title: Check Web Flows
use_cases.description: Open pages, follow basic navigation, capture screenshots, and verify visible states during manual test review.

use_cases.title: Inspect Page Structure
use_cases.description: Select page elements and collect their visible text, attributes, HTML, and parent context for debugging.

use_cases.title: Review Web Content
use_cases.description: Navigate public pages, summarize visible content, and preserve screenshots for later comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Open A Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the web-browser skill to start a fresh browser, open [URL], and tell me whether the page loads correctly.

prompt_templates.title: List Important Links
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to [URL], count visible links, and list the most important navigation labels with their destinations.

prompt_templates.title: Capture A UI State
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], perform [steps], take a screenshot, and summarize the visible state and any errors.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Interactive Elements
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the element picker on [URL] for [task]. Return the selected element details and suggest a reliable selector.

output_examples.input: Check whether the pricing page loads and capture evidence.
output_examples.output: The pricing page opened in the active tab, the main navigation was visible, and a screenshot file was created for review.

output_examples.input: Inspect the sign-up button on the home page.
output_examples.output: Selected element: a button with visible sign-up text, a primary action class, and parent context from the hero section.

output_examples.input: Count links that leave the current domain.
output_examples.output: The page contained fourteen visible links. Three links left the current domain and were grouped by destination.

best_practices: Use a fresh browser profile unless logged-in state is required for the task.
Open only trusted URLs and close the browser when the review is complete.
Treat screenshots, selected element data, and evaluation output as sensitive when logged in.
anti_patterns: Do not use the profile option with personal accounts unless the session risk is accepted.
Do not leave the Chrome remote debugging port open after the task finishes.
Do not paste untrusted JavaScript into the evaluation helper.

faq.question: Does this skill browse the public web?
faq.answer: Yes. It controls a local Chrome browser, so opened pages can make normal web requests.

faq.question: Does it require Google Chrome?
faq.answer: Yes. The start script uses the macOS Google Chrome application path and Chrome DevTools Protocol.

faq.question: Can it use my logged-in sessions?
faq.answer: Yes, only when the profile option is used. That option copies cookies and logins into a working profile.

faq.question: Does it send data to an external server?
faq.answer: The helper scripts connect to localhost. The websites opened in Chrome can make their own network requests.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It saves the active viewport as a screenshot in the system temporary directory.

faq.question: Is automatic installation recommended?
faq.answer: No. Review is recommended because the skill uses process execution, filesystem access, browser profile copying, and CDP control.
